built.guards:
vhi_guard.open_run(cut) runs before any read:
- The CUT is the first instant that may not be read.
- CUT > 2026-01-01 is always refused (GuardError).
- CUT > 2022-01-01 is refused unless LOOK_DECLARED is a readable file whose text contains the word "declared" (case-insensitive regex \bdeclared\b).
- Only for such a CUT is the one access line appended, and it is appended before anything is read. Any CUT <= 2022-01-01 writes nothing (log_access raises). One CUT per process.

The read guard is installed for the whole process on pandas.read_parquet, pandas.read_csv and pyarrow.parquet.read_table. Lens and strategy modules call these through their module attribute, so they are covered too. It refuses:
- lab/holdout_raw, lab/data/holdout, and any data file whose name carries 2026;
- any lab/data parquet without the filter ts < t, t <= CUT;
- any parquet under lab/results without the filter entry_time < t, t <= CUT (all trades files, official and lens outputs);
- raw data CSVs.

As a result, nq_btc_follow's default leader loader, which would read us100 to 2025, raises instead of reading.

The readers add more: official results are read with entry_time < CUT and exit_time < CUT, so no result realised after the CUT is materialised. The full-period attrs of the official trades files are dropped.

recalc.sleeves() is called once. synthesis_B and payoff receive that registry in memory, so every component calls the same make_orders objects (asserted before each build). The leader is set through the nq function's own globals and asserted to end before the CUT.
built.extending:
Add a sleeve line to look_spec.json, put its key in a portfolio, add a comparison, rehearse, declare, then run look.py once.

1. Existing change kinds:
   - k1_riskbp (q, purge_days, min_train, labels_mode, declared_T);
   - payoff (family S with k and reentry true/false/'n/a', T with m, H with j, B with b) on any sleeve;
   - new: a frozen rule on another instrument.
   Portfolios can be written relative to P0: {"replace": {old: new}, "add": [...], "drop": [...]}.

2. A new change that skips signals before the simulation (a skipped signal never blocks the sleeve): write a function decorated with vhi_sleeves.register_change("kind") taking (spec, mk, O, mode, ctx) and returning (kept orders, {"diag": ...}). List its file in spec "plugins". Example: example_plugins.skip_ny_hours.

3. An Addendum I stake rule (per trade or per sleeve):
   - Write a class with .stakes(trades, ctx) -> multipliers, where 0 means not taken and the chain is unchanged. ctx carries cut, mode, exec, sleeve, sym, book (every sleeve's paper trades, for "agreement"), signals (per-signal tables: decision/fill time, riskbp, label alone, exit alone) and purge.
   - Use vhi_stakes.yearly_refit for the 1 January refits; a fit for year Y may only use outcomes known before 1 January Y minus 7 days.
   - Reference it as portfolios[P].stakes[sleeve] = {"kind": "python", "module": "<file>", "factory": "<class>", "args": {...}}. Built-in kinds: const, sleeve_year ({year: m}, e.g. Addendum I weights), trade_table (a parquet of entry_time, side, stake), wf_terciles (a descriptor of the signal table). Example: example_plugins.HourBandStake.
   - Set "signals": true on the sleeve if the rule needs the signal table.

4. Rehearse with proofs.py or look.py --cut 2022-01-01. Check the in-sample numbers against the lens that found the change (add a proof against its published file), then declare the spec (ideally quoting its sha256, which look.py records) and run the look once.
caveats: The look was not run. LOOK_DECLARED was never set and val_access.log has no autopsy_HI_look line. The harness ran only at CUT 2022-01-01 and 2021-01-01 (both in sample). The CUT 2026 path is the same code: proof k shows that moving the CUT changes no completed trade. Not exercised: frames to 2025, which need about 1.6x the time and memory (the in-sample run takes about 75 s).

The live semantics must be declared. 'As the live program would' leaves open how the robot decides a sleeve is flat. The default 'entry_bar' (the verifiers' way, the one quoted in synthesis_B) re-simulates the chain with the live exits and tests one position at the delayed entry bar. 'rule' keeps the rule's own test, so a signal at the exit minute stays ignored. 'lab_chain' executes only the lab chain's trades. K2 in sample, FP: 391 / +141.8 R, 389 / +138.7 R and 344 / +103.3 R respectively. The last shows how much re-entering after the Friday close matters.

Live, literally applied to us100: the hands close at 23:50 server (16:50 New York), when us100 is already shut (about 16:15 New York). A us100 position still open then (only possible for variants that hold over a weekend, such as ocm4 T1) is closed at the Sunday reopen, 'at the first opportunity'. The live 3-spread refusal uses the open spread of the live fill bar; the verifier used the close spread (same result in sample).

Each sleeve keeps its lens's convention, and the two differ. sB (synthesis_B, breadth, sizing) uses the iterative 3-spread refusal and drops trades still open at the frame end. payoff refuses before the simulation and uses the lens's censoring. P0 uses sB; the payoff variants use payoff; the references agree in sample.

Payoff censoring for crypto is generalised. The lens keeps a 'time' exit at the frame's last bar because its in-sample crypto frames end inside the weekend closure. The look's CUT, 2026-01-01, is a Wednesday evening in New York, so the harness censors such exits whenever the CUT is not inside the closure. In sample this gives 0 differences. At CUT 2021 it removes one artificial brk72 btcusd exit per run that the lens's rule would have kept.

K1's walk-forward labels use the run's own cost mode (synthesis_B did this: x1.5 labels in x1.5). The declaration text says FP labels; the thresholds are identical either way. The option labels_mode 'fp' exists if the lead wants the declaration's wording.

The capped account matters for P2. In sample (FP, 2018-02..2021-12) the 6/2 caps refuse 964 P2 entries against 328 for P0: P2 makes +981.1 R capped against +1,153.2 R as a plain sum (weekly Sharpe 3.38 vs 3.34). The orb crypto sleeves compete for the 2 slots per market. Live, P0 falls from +788.6 to +670.8 R and P2 from +1,153.2 to +970.9 R (FP, plain sum).

Weeks follow synthesis_B: from the week of the window start to the week of its end minus 1 minute, every week counted. The look's first week (27 Dec 2021 - 2 Jan 2022) is therefore always zero. By-year weekly measures follow the sizing lenses' Thursday rule, clipped to the window's years, so no exit is lost at the end of 2025.

The Addendum I stake rules are not written yet. The harness gives the interface and examples, which are not candidates. Generic walk-forward stakes train on outcomes whose alone exit falls before 1 January minus 7 days, stricter than K1's 'decided before'.

Values that include a 2022 exit are not reproduced or quoted: synthesis_B's totR_official for donch4h and orb gold (84.235 and 230.065) includes a 2022 exit, so only rows closed before the CUT are compared. In proof f the cluster lens's trades reader was replaced in memory by the same read with the entry_time filter. No lens file was edited.

The lead's periodic commits ('Agents' work in progress') included the harness files; I ran no git command that changes anything. The proof script's check subprocesses (look.py rehearsals and refusals) ran while the parent process waited, one heavy process at a time.
